caption: The drawing depicts a formal garden layout viewed from above. The upper section contains a large, roughly rectangular garden with intricate, symmetrical geometric patterns divided into four primary triangular sections, each with diagonal and curved pathways bordered by green hedges. Each triangular section contains smaller plant beds, shaded in pink and gray, with a circular area and a tree in the center of each. Additional trees line the garden’s outer border. In the center of the rectangular garden is a circular feature, colored pink, possibly representing a fountain or statue. To the lower left of this main garden is another garden section divided into three triangular beds with similar hedged borders and central circular areas, each containing a tree. These triangular beds also alternate between shaded pink and green plantings. Between the two gardens, there is a rectangular structure with a blue-gray roof, red rectangles on the roof, and steps leading down to the gardens, likely representing a building or pavilion. Pathways in a light tan color connect all areas, leading towards the bottom edge of the image, which features a shoreline bordered by beige cliffs and blue water labeled “EAST RIVER.” Green lawns and small scattered trees fill the surrounding space, with a denser grouping of trees and dark green shading in the upper left of the drawing.
title: Ketteltas Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
